title: PRD interlock conveyor: clarify scope, acceptance lanes, and cross-team signoff path
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Summary: This ticket establishes a concrete signoff conveyor for the Private Deployments PRD v1.2. The goal is to remove ambiguity around acceptance lanes for engineering, design, and legal, limit scope for the MVP, and surface gating criteria for data residency and KMS integration. Deliverables: (1) a single-page acceptance matrix for the PRD, (2) a scoped feature checklist that can ship within Dedicated/Private Q4, (3) a cross-team review cadence and handoff doc with owners and SLAs, (4) a list of blocking items for the Security/Legal review with proposed mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering: End-to-end e2e validation for model serving inside customer VPC with network isolation verified via staging runbook
Design: Console UX flows for private deployment onboarding approved and annotated Figma screens with error/fallback states
Legal/Security: Data residency and KMS key lifecycle doc reviewed and either signed or an explicit mitigation path (timelines + fallback) agreed
Rollout: Canary target (10% traffic) and automatic fallback policy documented with rollback playbook
Telemetry: Minimum set of traces and metrics (latency, error rate, token-cost delta) instrumented and visible in Console dashboards
notes: Rationale: Multiple teams reported ambiguous exit criteria during the last Private beta. This ticket contains the 'conveyor' plan: discrete signoff gates with clear owners so a scope change or legal blocker doesn't silently delay rollout. We've proposed a reduced MVP that removes live-rotation of keys (defer to post-MVP) to reduce legal surface area.
tradeoffs: Trade-off chosen: scope reduction (defer key rotation automation) improves time-to-ship and reduces legal complexity, but requires a documented manual rotation SOP and a follow-up ticket for automation. Alternative (full automation) was estimated >3 additional sprints and flagged high-risk by Security during triage.
decisions: MVP scope will exclude automated KMS rotation (manual SOP required) - decided 2025-10-06 by PM/SEC/ENG
Canary will be 10% traffic for 72 hours with preflight load test - decided 2025-10-09
Design will provide annotated fallback states for two network-failure modes by 2025-10-14
open_questions: Does Legal accept the proposed manual KMS SOP as an interim mitigation for customers with strict rotation policies?
Which Dedicated capacity pools are acceptable as canary targets (low latency vs. regional compliance)?
Are there any regulatory jurisdictions we must explicitly exclude in the initial private rollout?
